title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree, identify the lowest common ancestor of two specified nodes.
statement: Given a binary tree, identify the lowest common ancestor of two specified nodes. The LCA is the deepest node that has both specified nodes as descendants, including the nodes themselves as descendants.
constraints: The input contains 2–100 TreeNode objects with unique values from -10^9 through 10^9; it is an arbitrary binary tree, not necessarily a search tree.
p and q are different existing nodes selected by their values. Return their actual lowest common ancestor node, counting a node as its own descendant, without changing the input tree.

hints: You need a way to move upward from both selected nodes even though TreeNode has no parent field.
Traverse once to record each visited node's parent until both p and q have been found.
Collect p and all of its ancestors, then move q upward until it enters that set.
Use node identity, not only values; return the actual shared ancestor from root and do not alter the tree.
editorial: An iterative traversal builds parent links only until both selected object references are discovered. Every ancestor of p is placed in a set; the first ancestor reached while climbing from q is the lowest shared one. A recursive approach also fits the stated tree size. The independent oracle compares the targets' binary paths rather than constructing parent pointers.

Node 5 contains node 4 in its subtree and counts as its own descendant, so the answer is node 5.
